title: Attic Orators
description: Advanced reading and study of Attic orators such as Demosthenes, Lysias, Aeschines, and Isocrates, with attention to the language, style, and rhetoric of the speeches, and to their political and historical context.

title: Lucian
description: Advanced reading and study of selected passages from Lucian, with attention to the language and style of his satirical dialogues, and to their social and historical context.

title: Greek Novel
description: Advanced reading and study of selected chapters of an ancient Greek novel, with attention to the language and style of the work and to its literary, social and political contexts.

title: Greek Biography
description: Advanced reading and study of selections from Greek texts that focus on the 'lives' of notable figures (such as Xenophon's Cyropaedia, Plutarch's Lives, and the Life of Aesop). Attention is paid to the language and style of the works, as well to the genre of 'biography'.

title: Pre-Socratic Philosophers
description: Advanced readings in the first "formal" philosophers of the Western tradition. Normally includes all the major pre-Socratics (Parmenides, Heraclitus, Pythagoras, Xenophones, Anaxagoras, Democritus) and their contributions to European thought. Sometimes concentrates upon thinkers of the fifth-century Sophistic Movement.

title: Greek Prose Composition
description: Improves active knowledge of the Greek language, both grammar and vocabulary, through careful writing. Refines a feeling for the Greek employed in various genres of Greek literature. Demonstrates how a feel for style helps interpret and explicate Greek literature.

title: Plato
description: Advanced reading of one or several Platonic dialogues from the early or middle period (Laches, Protagoras, Phaedo, Gorgias, Symposium), both as masterpieces of Greek literature and as philosophical dialogues.

title: Post-Platonic Philosophers
description: Advanced reading of selections from the more famous works of Aristotle (Nicomachean Ethics, Politics, De Anima, Metaphysics), emphasizing Aristotle both as thinker and as stylist; occasionally excerpts from Theophrastus, the Stoics, Plotinus.

title: Euripides
description: Advanced reading, translation, and discussion of a complete tragedy of Euripides, with attention to language, meter, staging, tragic themes and conventions, and the cultural context of Athenian drama, with an introduction to current scholarship.

title: Sophocles
description: Advanced reading, translation, and discussion of a complete tragedy of Sophocles, with attention to language, meter, staging, tragic themes and conventions, and the cultural context of Athenian drama, with an introduction to current scholarship.

title: Aeschylus
description: Advanced reading, translation, and discussion of a complete tragedy of Aeschylus, with attention to language, meter, staging, tragic themes and conventions, and the cultural context of Athenian drama, with an introduction to current scholarship.

title: Aristophanes
description: Advanced reading, translation, and discussion of a complete comedy of Aristophanes, with attention to language, meter, staging, comic themes and conventions, and the cultural context of Athenian drama, with an introduction to current scholarship.

title: Homer
description: Advanced reading and study of selections from the Iliad and/or Odyssey.

title: Hesiod, Theognis, and Solon
description: Advanced reading and study in the archaic poets.

title: Herodotus
description: Advanced reading and study in the histories of Herodotus.

title: Thucydides
description: Advanced reading and research in the historical, literary, and philological aspects of Thucydides.

title: Xenophon
description: Advanced reading and study in selected works.

title: Polybius
description: Selections from the great history, focusing either on the Hellenistic world of the later third century, the Punic Wars, or Rome's interventions across the Adriatic from 229 to 146 B.C. Translation and historical/ historiographical study.

title: Lyric Poets and Homeric Hymns
description: Advanced reading and study of lyric poems and Homeric hymns.

title: Pindar
description: Advanced reading, interpretation, metrical study, and textual criticism. Introduction to other choral poets.

title: Hellenistic Poets
description: Advanced study in poetry of the Alexandrian period, normally concentrating upon a single major poet such as Apollonius, Callimachus, or Theocritus, with attention to language, meter, generic innovation, cultural context, and formative influence upon Latin literature. Includes introduction to current scholarship.

title: Elementary Hebrew
description: The beginning course in Hebrew. Starting with the study of the alphabet, the student is initiated into the rudiments of the language. Basic grammar, vocabulary, and conversation.

title: Elementary Hebrew

title: Intermediate Modern Hebrew
description: Continuation of Hebrew 3 with emphasis in writing, composition, and reading of Hebrew newspapers. Introduction to modern Hebrew literature: prose and poetry.

title: Intermediate Modern Hebrew

title: Intermediate Modern Hebrew

title: Readings in Modern Hebrew Prose and Poetry
description: Improve language ability and acquire knowledge in Hebrew literature. Readings/analyzing texts of modern and contemporary major Hebrew writers. Relationships between land, people and history, social, political, spiritual, and gender issues; impact of war.

title: World History
description: Survey of the peoples, cultures, and social, economic, and political systems that have characterized the world's major civilizations in Europe, Asia, Africa, the Americas, and Oceania from prehistory to 1000 CE.
